register: # SOURCE: ABB/FIMER 'Modbus RTU Register Map - Version Gt03.0, TRIO-50.0/60.0-TL-OUTD / TRIO-TM-50.0-400 / TRIO-TM-60.0-480 (rev 3.4, 2019)' (vendor document). ABB's tables give 1-based Modbus Data Addresses and state that the PDU address on the wire is one less, so every CSV register here is the table address minus 1 (each note shows the table address).
# APPLIES TO: TRIO-50.0/60.0-TL-OUTD (EU/US/JP). The TM-only DC inputs 2 and 3 are not mapped here because a TL inverter answers them with exception 2; use abb_fimer_trio_tm_50_60 for the TM models.

# FUNCTION CODES: measurements are input registers (FC04). The holding map (FC03 read, FC06/FC16 write) has the heartbeat and grid measures plus ABB's documented controls, marked RW with ABB's range for write validation. Whether anything can actually be written is decided by the app's gates (transport write_enabled and the per-register W toggle in the web UI).

# BYTE ORDER: ABB 'Byte order: Big-endian'. U32 counters are high register first (the app default). Floats are ABB's 'SF32' = Word Swapped Floating Point (low register first), so each float row carries Register_Endian little_endian-CDAB. ABB's example: output power 20000 W is returned as registers 0x4000 0x469C.

# CONTROLS: power management has two independent blocks. Block 1 (holding 189-226) exists for backward compatibility with PVI-RS485-Modbus converters and ABB discourages it for new work; block 2 (holding 500-515) is the plant-controller block. Each block keeps its own configuration. Configure 500-505 before sending a block-2 set point. Set points revert at inverter power-off. Writing 0 to 1005 or 1006 switches that RS-485 port away from Modbus immediately, after which the gateway can no longer reach the inverter (use Aurora Manager Lite to restore it).

note: table 180; ABB read/write control. 0 = on, 1 = off. Acted on only if the Remote on/off function is enabled in the inverter.
table 181; ABB read/write control. Write 1 to remove a pending latch; the register then returns to 0. Latch reset after a grid fault is on by default only for the Japanese grid code.
table 190; ABB read/write control. Packed value: low byte N, high byte M, T = N x step + M x 10 ms (ABB Annex 9); step set by 197. Default 4 s.
table 191; ABB read/write control. Default 2 min.
table 198; ABB read/write control. Only 0, 128, 256 or 384 are valid (ABB Annex 8). Default 256.

documented_name: Block 1 Dynamic Power Factor Set Point
note: table 200; ABB read/write control. -1..-0.001 over-excited (capacitive) or 0.001..1 under-excited (inductive); 0 is not valid. Dynamic: reverts to the default when the timeout register expires. IEEE-754 float, word-swapped (low register first).

documented_name: Block 1 Permanent Power Factor Set Point
note: table 202; ABB read/write control. -1..-0.001 or 0.001..1. Permanent: stored in the inverter's memory; ABB warns that writing permanent set points continuously can damage that memory, so use dynamic set points for regulation. IEEE-754 float, word-swapped (low register first).

documented_name: Block 1 Reset Reactive Power / PF Management
note: table 205; ABB read/write control. Write 1 to force reactive power to zero (PF = 1); the register then returns to 0.

documented_name: Block 1 Dynamic Active Power Set Point
note: table 210; ABB read/write control. Active power curtailment as a percentage of nominal power. Dynamic: reverts to the default when the timeout register expires.

documented_name: Block 1 Permanent Active Power Set Point
note: table 212; ABB read/write control. Active power curtailment as a percentage of nominal power. Permanent: stored in the inverter's memory; ABB warns that writing permanent set points continuously can damage that memory, so use dynamic set points for regulation.
table 215; ABB read/write control. Write 1 to force active power back to nominal; the register then returns to 0.

documented_name: Block 1 Dynamic Reactive Power Set Point (cos phi)
note: table 220; ABB read/write control. Negative = over-excited, positive = under-excited. Dynamic: reverts to the default when the timeout register expires. IEEE-754 float, word-swapped (low register first).

documented_name: Block 1 Permanent Reactive Power Set Point (cos phi)
note: table 222; ABB read/write control. Negative = over-excited, positive = under-excited. Permanent: stored in the inverter's memory; ABB warns that writing permanent set points continuously can damage that memory, so use dynamic set points for regulation. IEEE-754 float, word-swapped (low register first).

documented_name: Block 1 Dynamic Reactive Power Set Point (%)
note: table 225; ABB read/write control. Percentage of maximum apparent power; negative = over-excited. Dynamic: reverts to the default when the timeout register expires.

documented_name: Block 1 Permanent Reactive Power Set Point (%)
note: table 227; ABB read/write control. Percentage of maximum apparent power; negative = over-excited. Permanent: stored in the inverter's memory; ABB warns that writing permanent set points continuously can damage that memory, so use dynamic set points for regulation.
